author: orchestrating session (integration-time fix, not a dispatched workstream)
purpose: Closes the NEW_COUPLED_BLOCKER_DISCOVERED finding Workstream B raised while revalidating BLOCKER-2 (docs/phase-3f1-6-rx-final-blocker-closure/04-operative-supersession-remediation.json): lib/contract-model/analysis/orchestrator.ts built operativeSourceText from raw text with zero supersession check and hardcoded operativeLineage to null, defeating the safety checks Workstreams A/B/C/D/E just hardened. This fell in the gap between Workstream B's remit (BLOCKERS 2-6, forbidden from touching orchestrator.ts) and Workstream H's remit (BLOCKER-10 + AUDIT-F1/F2/F3/F6/F7 - none of which explicitly named this file's own supersession wiring); Workstream H's completed deliverable did not address it (confirmed by diff and by grep for operativeSourceText/operativeLineage in its own commits).

rootCauseFoundBeyondWhatWorkstreamBDocum.whatWorkstreamBReported: operativeSourceText built with zero supersession check; operativeLineage hardcoded null.
rootCauseFoundBeyondWhatWorkstreamBDocum.deeperRootCauseFoundDuringThisClosure: The orchestrator computes operativeState per instrument but NEVER used it to build a NodeSupersessionIndex, and NEVER passed one to runDiscoveryPipeline (which defaults to EMPTY_SUPERSESSION_INDEX per discovery/pipeline.ts's own signature). This means every real DiscoveredCandidate.supersessionStatus silently resolved UNKNOWN_SUPERSESSION_STATUS in live production regardless of real amendment data - which ALSO made Workstream B's own context-retrieval fix (buildCovenantContextBundle reading candidate.supersessionStatus to degrade sufficiencyState) inert end-to-end in the one place that actually runs live, since a candidate could never legitimately resolve KNOWN_SUPERSEDED there either. Fixing the index-wiring gap at its single source closes the whole live chain in one place, rather than patching each downstream symptom separately.

fix.change1_supersessionIndexWiring: After computing operativeState (per instrument), build a real NodeSupersessionIndex via buildNodeSupersessionIndex (reused from lib/contract-model/compiler/amendment/operative-state.ts, never re-implemented) when unit.baseDocumentId and operativeState are both present, else EMPTY_SUPERSESSION_INDEX (the codebase's own documented fail-closed default). Pass this index into runDiscoveryPipeline's own existing (previously always-omitted) 4th parameter.
fix.change2_operativeLineageDerivation: New deriveOperativeLineage(candidate, supersessionIndex, instrumentKey, asOfDate) helper: for each of a candidate's structuralNodeIds, calls the existing getNodeSupersessionStatus primitive and combines results worst-first (mirroring discovery/pass-d-reconcile.ts's own combineSupersessionForNodes convention, reused rather than re-derived), then maps the resolved NodeSupersessionStatus to a real OperativeLineageRef: KNOWN_SUPERSEDED -> OPERATIVE_STATE_CONFLICTED (forces semantic/normalize.ts's enforceSufficiencyConsistency to downgrade sufficiency regardless of what the compiler itself concluded), UNKNOWN_SUPERSESSION_STATUS -> OPERATIVE_STATE_REVIEW_REQUIRED (downgrades COMPLETE), CURRENT_OPERATIVE -> OPERATIVE_STATE_RESOLVED (no forced downgrade). Replaces the previous hardcoded operativeLineage: null.

whyThisIsRootCauseNotSymptomPatching: No compensating check was added at the operativeSourceText call site itself (e.g. blanking the text when superseded) - that would only mask the symptom for one field. Instead, the actual missing wiring (a real supersession index that discovery, context-retrieval, and now operativeLineage all correctly assume exists) was supplied at its one true origin point. Every consumer downstream of discovery (Workstream B's context-retrieval fix included) now receives a genuinely computed supersessionStatus in live production, not merely in its own isolated unit tests.

scopeDiscipline: Touches only lib/contract-model/analysis/orchestrator.ts. No test file was modified to accommodate this fix (all 1702 relevant tests already pass unmodified against it) - the fix is additive wiring, not a behavior change any existing test asserted against. No package-specific logic; reuses only already-certified-scope-general primitives (buildNodeSupersessionIndex, getNodeSupersessionStatus, EMPTY_SUPERSESSION_INDEX) that Workstreams A-E of Phase 3F.1.5.R/3F.1.6.R already built and this codebase already exercises elsewhere.
dispositionRationale: Closes the NEW_COUPLED_BLOCKER_DISCOVERED gap Workstream B raised for BLOCKER-2 at its actual root (a missing supersession-index wiring in the one live orchestration boundary), verified against the full relevant test suite including every test Workstream H's own AUDIT-F1/F2/F3/F6/F7/BLOCKER-10 work added. Per this phase's own charter, this closure does not self-certify - independent verification of this specific fix (a fresh adversarial KNOWN_SUPERSEDED candidate reaching the live orchestrator end-to-end, confirming operativeLineage.operativeStatus is genuinely OPERATIVE_STATE_CONFLICTED and the compiler's own sufficiency is downgraded accordingly) is explicitly named as required evidence for Part B's BLOCKER-2 recertification section.
